metadata.name: Mercury RAG Evaluation Test Set
metadata.description: Test cases for evaluating RAG retrieval and generation quality

test_cases.expected_answer: Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) is a computational method used for simulating fluid flows. It is a meshfree Lagrangian method where the fluid is represented by particles that carry properties such as mass, velocity, and energy.
ground_truth_contexts: SPH is a meshfree particle method
It uses kernel functions for interpolation

test_cases.query: How does kernel smoothing work in SPH?
test_cases.expected_answer: Kernel smoothing in SPH uses a smoothing kernel function to interpolate field values from neighboring particles. The kernel is a weighting function that gives more weight to nearby particles and less weight to distant particles.
ground_truth_contexts: Common kernels include cubic spline and Gaussian
Smoothing length determines the influence radius

test_cases.query: What are the advantages of SPH over grid-based methods?
test_cases.expected_answer: SPH has several advantages: it naturally handles free surfaces and interfaces, can easily track material interfaces, handles large deformations well, and is adaptive in resolution since particles can move freely.
ground_truth_contexts: Meshfree nature allows for natural handling of free surfaces
Adaptive resolution based on particle distribution

test_cases.query: What are common applications of SPH?
test_cases.expected_answer: SPH is commonly used for astrophysics simulations, fluid dynamics, coastal engineering, impact and explosion modeling, and computer graphics for visual effects.
ground_truth_contexts: Visual effects in movies and games

test_cases.query: What is the time complexity of SPH neighbor search?
test_cases.expected_answer: The time complexity of SPH neighbor search depends on the algorithm used. With spatial data structures like cell lists or tree structures, it can be reduced to O(N log N) or even O(N) for well-distributed particles.
ground_truth_contexts: Brute force neighbor search is O(N^2)
Cell lists and linked lists improve to O(N)
Tree structures like k-d trees provide O(N log N)

test_cases.query: Explain the continuity equation in SPH
test_cases.expected_answer: The continuity equation in SPH represents conservation of mass and is discretized using particle approximations. It relates the rate of density change to the velocity field and can be formulated in multiple ways for numerical stability.
ground_truth_contexts: Density summation vs continuity equation formulation
